slots.title: Energy inflation and the Fed’s rate decision
slots.body:
Brent crude settled at $104.61 on the session, down 2.8% from the prior close but still above the $100 mark cited in weekend policy discussion.

The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 5.0% on the latest curve snapshot, with the gap between 2-year and 10-year yields at 0.39 percentage points.

Bloomberg This Weekend featured PNC Chief Investment Officer Amanda Agati on energy-driven inflation complicating the Fed’s rate decision, with markets adjusting to a longer Iran conflict and still-strong corporate earnings in the background.

What part of the inflation print do you watch first when energy is moving like this?

slots.title: Trump timeline for Iran and oil above $100
slots.body:
CNBC quoted Trump expecting the Iran war to end soon after the midterms and oil to fall sharply after that.

On the same session, Brent was at $104.61 (−2.8%) and the United States Oil Fund ($USO) closed at $154.90 (−2.2%), after a week that left crude prices sharply higher despite Friday’s pullback.

The piece noted Brent above $104 and WTI above $100 on a weekly basis.

How do you separate headline risk on oil from the day-to-day price print?

slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 12, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,656.98, up 65.28 points (+0.9%), with an intraday range of 7,636.75–7,677.02.
The index remains below its 52-week high of 7,816.70 in the injected snapshot.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,333.03 (+1.0%, +251.31), session low 26,283.11 and high 26,431.22.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 509.19 points (+1.0%) to 52,573.29.

The Russell 2000 gained a smaller +0.4% to 2,903.94 (+13.00), versus the roughly 1% moves in the three large-cap benchmarks.

The VIX fell 2.00 to 15.84 (−11.2%), with a session low of 15.59 and high of 17.71 — a lower fear gauge on a day when equities closed firm.

Injected news referenced August inflation reporting (headline inflation unchanged, core inflation lower in one piece) and discussion of energy-driven inflation complicating Federal Reserve rate decisions; the economic calendar block for this payload was empty, so no new print was listed for Sept. 12 itself.

Oil-related quotes in the cross-asset set showed pullback at the close: Brent crude (BZUSD) at 104.61 (−2.8%, −3.02) and the United States Oil Fund (USO) at 154.90 (−2.2%, −3.48).
A CNBC headline in the feed noted oil prices pulled back Friday while Brent had been above $104 and WTI above $100 in the weekly context described there.

Gold futures (GCUSD) were nearly unchanged at 4,408.90 (0.0%, +1.60).
The dollar proxy UUP closed at 28.07 (+0.1%).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was flat at 77,260.70 (−0.0%) in the injected quote.

Treasury yield levels in the payload were dated 2026-09-10: 10-year 5.0%, 2-year 4.6%, 2s10s spread 0.39 percentage points — not restated as a Sept. 12 session move.

Among megacaps, Alphabet ($GOOGL) rose +1.8% to 338.50; Amazon ($AMZN) +1.9% to 256.78; Salesforce ($CRM) +1.9% to 247.72; Netflix ($NFLX) +1.8% to 77.40; Walmart ($WMT) +1.3% to 107.15; Procter & Gamble ($PG) +1.6% to 145.27.
UnitedHealth ($UNH) was an outlier at −2.4% (379.09).
NVIDIA ($NVDA) ended essentially flat at 218.29 (−0.0%).

Semiconductor and hardware names were mixed but mostly higher: AMD +2.5% to 516.13, Intel +2.6% to 102.94, TSM +1.2% to 433.24, ASML +0.6% to 1,698.30.

Overseas indexes in the bundle closed earlier: Nikkei 225 −1.9% to 64,011.34; Hang Seng −0.6% to 24,805.60; FTSE 100 +0.4% to 10,650.44.
